---
title: "Spatial covariates for mass valuation of agricultural land"
subtitle: "A reference dataset for Poltava oblast, Ukraine"
lang: en
---

## Objective

This project sets a baseline for computing spatial covariates for the mass valuation of agricultural land in Ukraine.

It builds a **reference dataset**: a fixed set of 1,000 simulated land parcels, with 81 spatial covariates per parcel, computed from a controlled set of inputs. Other implementations (other software, tools or teams) can run the same calculations on the same parcels and compare their results with this one.

The covariates cover four families:

| Family | Variables | What it measures | Page |
|-------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| Distance | 6 | Distance on the sphere to the nearest elevator, main road and local road, from the parcel centroid and from its edge | [Distance](distance.qmd) |
| Soil | 20 | Ten SoilGrids topsoil (0–30 cm) properties, as the parcel polygon mean and as the value at the centroid | [Soil](soil.qmd) |
| Relief | 6 | Elevation, slope and aspect exposure from the Copernicus 30 m DEM, over the whole parcel polygon | [Relief](relief.qmd) |
| Crop cover | 49 | Share of the parcel in 7 land-cover groups, for each year 2019–2025 | [Crop cover](crop.qmd) |

All 81 variables are listed on the [Output](output.qmd) page.

## Study area

The study area is **Poltava oblast** (COD-AB P-code `UA53`, English name in COD-AB "Poltavska"). It suits a reference test because it has:

- towns (Poltava, Kremenchuk, Lubny and others), where soil maps have no data;
- the Dnipro river and the Kremenchuk reservoir, where soil maps have no data and the DEM is flat;
- seven neighbouring oblasts, so that some parcels cross an oblast boundary;
- a band north of 50°N where the Copernicus DEM tiles have a coarser longitude spacing.

![Reference parcels (centroids), elevators and roads in Poltava oblast. Details on the [Reference inputs](reference.qmd) page.](../figures/parcels-map.png){fig-alt="Map of Poltava oblast with 1,000 parcel centroids coloured by case: interior parcels spread across the oblast, border parcels along its boundary, and nodata parcels clustered on grey soil-NoData areas, mostly along the Kremenchuk reservoir in the south-west. Thirty black triangles mark elevators, four long straight lines cross the oblast as main roads, and fifty short lines are local roads."}

## What the dataset is for

- **A gold standard.** The parcels, elevators and roads are simulated once and committed to the repository. They never change, so results from different tools can be compared row by row.
- **Hard cases on purpose.** 15 % of the parcels cross an oblast boundary and 15 % sit on soil NoData (towns, rivers, the reservoir), to test how each implementation handles edges and missing data.
- **Explicit methods.** Every choice (distance on the sphere, coverage-weighted polygon means, fill order for missing soil values, the 2025 crop rule) is documented on these pages, next to the code that implements it.

The output is one long table, `parcel_id | variable | value | source`, with 81,000 rows (see [Output](output.qmd)).

## Quick start

1. Clone the repository and open it in R (4.6 or later) from the project root.
2. Restore the packages:

   ```r
   renv::restore()
   ```

3. Set the paths to your own soil and crop rasters in `00-setup.R` (`soil_dir`, `crop_dir` and the eight `crop_*` file names). See [Data](data.qmd).
4. Download the public inputs (oblast boundaries and DEM tiles), once:

   ```r
   source("00b-download.R")
   ```

5. Run the scripts in order, each with `source()`. Every script sources `00-setup.R` itself.

   ```r
   source("02-diagnostics.R")
   source("03-distance.R")
   source("04-soil.R")
   source("05-relief.R")
   source("06-crop.R")
   source("07-crop-2025.R")
   source("21-combine.R")
   source("22-descriptives.R")
   ```

`01-simulate-reference.R` is **not** part of the normal run. It created the committed reference inputs once and aborts if they already exist. The full run order, with inputs and outputs, is on the [Pipeline](pipeline.qmd) page.

## Repository

Code: <https://github.com/EBukin/ukrMassValuationSpatialExtract>. The repository ships no external data: soil and crop rasters are provided by the user, public inputs are downloaded by a script, and only the simulated reference inputs, the results and this website are committed.
